draft.title: Making inferences from a sample
card: An inference uses a sample's results to estimate something about the whole population, such as its mean (the average).
To find a sample mean, add up all the values and divide by how many there are. Example: 4, 6 and 8 add to 18, and 18 ÷ 3 = 6.
The sample mean is used as an estimate of the population mean. If the sample was a random one, the estimate is more reliable.
The estimate is uncertain. Another sample would probably give a slightly different mean, so the population mean is probably close to it but not exactly equal.
draft.remember: A sample mean is a good estimate of the population mean, but it is not certain to be exact.

a.q: A random sample of 5 students in Adelaide spend 20, 30, 10, 40 and 50 minutes on homework. What is the best estimate of the mean for all students in the school?
opts: 30 minutes
150 minutes
40 minutes
50 minutes
a.why: The values add to 150, and 150 ÷ 5 = 30 minutes. The total of 150 is tempting, but the dividing step was skipped.
a.clue: Add the values, then divide by how many there are.

b.q: A random sample of 4 Year 8 students in Cairns had a mean height of 160 cm. Another random sample of 4 had a mean of 164 cm. What does this show?
opts: Samples vary, so the population mean is only estimated
One of the samples must have been collected wrongly
The population mean is exactly 162 cm
The population mean cannot be estimated from samples
b.why: Different samples give different means, so any estimate is uncertain. Averaging the two to get 162 cm is tempting, but it is still only an estimate and not an exact value.
b.clue: Would two samples always give the same mean?

b.best: Samples vary, so the population mean is only estimated

problems.detail: The question says the sample is of 5 students in Adelaide, then asks about 'all students in the school', but no school has been named. It should say, for example, 'a random sample of 5 students at an Adelaide school'.
The remember line calls any sample mean a good estimate. The card says the estimate is more reliable only when the sample is random, and that condition is dropped.

check.summary: Both answers are correct (30 minutes; samples vary, so the mean is only estimated). Question a refers to 'the school' without naming one, and the remember line drops the card's point that random samples give more reliable estimates.
